entries.test: Musk's public statements from 2015 to 2022 giving roughly two-year timelines for full self-driving, and whether Tesla had shipped truly self-driving cars by May 2022.
entries.note: In context, 'it still hasn't happened' refers to Musk's promised Tesla self-driving, not to driverless cars from every company.

entries.test: Published 2022-era evidence on whether data-driven AI systems performed much worse on rare or out-of-distribution cases than on common ones.
entries.note: 'Very serious' is vague, but there is a shared empirical reading about failures on rare cases.

entries.test: Whether Tesla's 2022 driving stack was mainly deep-learning-based and had documented failures in unusual situations, such as the summoned Model Y hitting a parked jet.
entries.note: Calling deep learning a 'glorified hash-table-like lookup' is his own loaded description, and he hedges with 'so far as I know'.
The claim about the future is hedged with 'probably'. The firm part about the present is close to the long-tail claim above.

entries.test: Whether any system widely accepted as AGI is reached while still relying heavily on deep learning.
entries.note: 'Have to' states a necessity for reaching AGI (the next sentence makes this explicit); it is not an ought. The proposition leaves out the AGI goal.
It mixes a personal assessment ('seems unrealistic to me') with a need for 'more techniques' and never says what they are needed for.
'Might well not' is hedged language about possibility.

entries.test: Whether general-purpose domestic robots remain far behind road-driving autonomy in demonstrated capability and deployment.
entries.note: This compares how hard two problems are, so it can only be checked through what has actually been achieved and deployed.
'That methodological problem' and 'a good proposal' are too vague for readers to agree on a test.

entries.test: The 2022 state of interpretability and model-debugging research, and whether fixes to deep learning failures relied mainly on more data and bigger models.
entries.note: 'Nobody' and 'wicked hard' are exaggerated. The substance can be checked against the research of the time.

entries.test: Whether, by the end of 2029, an AI can read a novel and reliably answer non-literal questions about plot, character, conflicts and motivations.
entries.note: This is one of five bet criteria. The bet is won only if a single system beats three of them.

entries.test: Whether, by the end of 2029, an AI can convert arbitrary natural-language proofs from the mathematical literature into formally verifiable form, e.g. Lean.
entries.note: 'Arbitrary' sets a high bar: converting selected proofs would not count.
